catalogue_scope: A fixed known-exact binary-correspondence catalogue for the original directed f/T rows; not a complete classification of all possible algebraic relations.
not_designated_meaning: Not listed in this catalogue; does not assert mathematical independence or absence of any relation.
comparison_formula_meaning: For not_designated rows this is the specific candidate equation inherited from the original map, not an asserted identity.
search_policy: No new affine-formula enumeration or synthetic input search; no unproved consistent candidate promoted to other_known_exact.

proofs.descent_inverse: Recoil count is the descent count of the inverse. Applying inverse twice recovers pi, so recoils(pi^-1)=descents(pi).
proofs.peak_complement: C(pi)_i=n+1-pi_i reverses every strict comparison. Each interior peak of pi is exactly a valley of C(pi).
proofs.exceedance_inverse: The bijection i -> j=pi_i sends each pi_i>i to pi^-1_j=i<j, and conversely. Exceedances(pi)=deficiencies(pi^-1).
proofs.subsequence_complement: For each fixed subsequence of indices, complement reverses all value inequalities; increasing subsequences of pi correspond to decreasing subsequences of C(pi), with equal lengths.
proofs.run_complement: Complement reverses adjacent comparisons on every contiguous interval; maximal increasing-run length of pi equals maximal decreasing-run length of C(pi).
proofs.record_complement: pi_i exceeds all preceding values iff C(pi)_i is below all preceding values. Left-to-right maxima and minima thus correspond.
proofs.decomposition_complement: A global descent cut has every prefix value greater than every suffix value. After complement the prefix comprises {1,...,k}, exactly a direct-sum component cut. A nonempty permutation has one more component than component cuts, so components(C(pi))=global_descents(pi)+1.
proofs.reverse_max: Transposition sends the outdegree of each vertex to its indegree. Taking the maximum gives max_in(R(A))=max_out(A).
proofs.reverse_min: Transposition sends the outdegree of each vertex to its indegree. Taking the minimum gives min_in(R(A))=min_out(A).
proofs.complement_out: Off-diagonal complement sends every outdegree d to n-1-d. Therefore min_out(C(A))=n-1-max_out(A).
proofs.complement_in: Off-diagonal complement sends every indegree d to n-1-d. Therefore min_in(C(A))=n-1-max_in(A).

excluded_scope: Self-task candidates, identities using three or more tasks, conditional/nonlinear identities and exhaustive independence claims are outside this catalogue.
